findings.quote: COMPARISON HEADING: How does Aruba compare to neighbouring and nearby countries?
findings.problem: 16 of the 20 partial-data pages keep a comparison heading, although these places have no score, no rank and no comparison table (the accepted rule), so the heading promises a comparison that is not there (ABW, AIA, ALA, AND, ASM and others). CCK and CXR are labelled 'Partial data' in TITLE and H1, yet their HERO says 'What we do have No independent source covers this place yet.'
findings.expected: Drop the comparison heading on partial pages; label zero-source places as 'no data' rather than 'partial data'.
findings.verification: opus: The live dist/client/en/country/abw/index.html renders the heading together with a real table (Aruba 'Partial data' row plus Grenada and Dominican Republic). The extractor only dropped the rows because the grey row has a colspan, so the heading does not promise a missing table. The CCK 'partial data' label with zero sources is at most a cosmetic point.

findings.quote: COMPARISON HEADING: How does Guadeloupe compare to neighbouring and nearby countries?
findings.problem: All 18 partial-data pages (no score, no rank and no comparison table by design) still carry a 'How does X compare to neighbouring and nearby countries?' heading, so the page promises a comparison it does not show. On NFK, FAQ 1 ends with the boilerplate '[B7] Read the government advisories below and check your own government's travel advice before you go.', but FAQ 3 says 'no government in our dataset publishes a travel advisory for Norfolk Island', so there are no advisories below to read.
findings.expected: Hide the comparison heading on partial-data pages. On NFK, replace the 'advisories below' pointer with a line such as 'No government advisory is on record; check your own government's guidance.'
findings.verification: owner correction 2026-10-15: By design, not a defect: a grey (partial-data) place keeps its neighbour comparison table, with its own row shown as 'Partial data' next to scored neighbours (src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows). The audit brief wrongly listed 'no comparison table' among the accepted grey-page traits, and the verifier confirmed against that brief. Verifier had said: The heading half is wrong: the full GLP/NFK pages do show a comparison table (neighbours with scores, the place itself as 'Partial data'), so the heading does not promise something missing. The NFK half is real: FAQ1 says 'Read the government advisories below...' while FAQ3 says 'no government in our dataset publishes a travel advisory for Norfolk Island', so no advisories are below. Confirmed only for the NFK pointer.

findings.quote: The main concern is violent crime: 5.1 homicides per 100,000 people (World Bank, 2021).
findings.problem: A SUMMARY dated 15 October 2026 uses a 2021 homicide figure as its headline 'main concern'. LUX uses 2022 in the same slot ('the lowest-rated is violent crime: 1.5 homicides per 100,000 people (World Bank, 2022).'), while the six pages that cite a year for this indicator use 2023. The year is labelled, so nothing is misdated, but two headlines rest on figures four to five years old.
findings.expected: Use the latest World Bank year for the indicator on every page (2023 where it exists), or say in the headline that the figure is from an earlier year.
findings.verification: opus: The raw World Bank data (data/raw/2026-10-15/worldbank-parsed.json) shows that 2021 is the latest available year for LIE (5.12) and 2022 for LUX (1.53). The pages already use the latest value and label the year, so the proposed fix is impossible. The real issue is a different one: LIE's 5.1 is a small-population spike (about 2 homicides, up from 2.6 the previous year) that becomes the headline 'main concern'. That is a noise or headline-selection problem, not stale data.

findings.quote: even its weakest area, crime, scores 8.0/10, well inside the low-risk band
findings.problem: On this site 8.0/10 is labelled 'Very low risk' (GRC at 8.0/10 is 'classified as Very low risk'), while 'Low risk' covers 7 up to 8. An 8.0 pillar is therefore not 'well inside the low-risk band'.
findings.expected: Use band words that match the composite labels, for example 'at the top of the low-risk range', or simply give the 8.0/10 value.
findings.verification: opus: Pillar bands are not the composite bands. Across all en pages the pillar 'Low' label covers 7.0 to 9.3 (e.g. LUX 'Crime (8.0/10 · Low', GRC 'Conflict (8.3/10 · Low'), and there is no 'Very low' at pillar level. A pillar at 8.0 is therefore inside the pillar low-risk band, and the sentence matches the page's own pillar label.

findings.quote: COMPARISON HEADING: How does Puerto Rico compare to neighbouring and nearby countries?
findings.problem: Partial-data pages (PRI, SJM, SXM, TCA, VAT, UMI, VGB, VIR, WLF, XKX, SMR, REU, all showing 'no official safety score') still carry a 'How does X compare to neighbouring and nearby countries?' heading, but no comparison content appears under it in the batch. The page says these places get no comparison, so the heading promises one that is not there.
findings.expected: Hide the comparison heading on places with no score, or show one plain line saying no comparison is available.
findings.verification: opus: The heading is real, but the claim that nothing follows it is false. PRI, SJM, SXM, TCA, VAT, UMI, VGB, VIR, WLF, XKX, SMR and REU all show a filled comparison table: a 'Partial data' row for the place plus scored neighbours or 'nearby' countries. The finding misread the batch. Separately, showing a table at all on partial pages may go against the stated 'no comparison table' design, but that is a different issue.

findings.quote: Thin or stale data pulls a country's score toward a cautious regional baseline instead of guessing
findings.problem: Boilerplate [B13] is inserted into the Q1 answer of pages with full data. NZL HERO shows '100% data coverage', and so do SGP, SVK and UKR. The sentence therefore implies thin or stale data that the page does not have, and it sits mid-answer between unrelated sentences.
findings.expected: Show [B13] only when coverage is below threshold or a source is stale. Otherwise leave it out of the answer.
findings.verification: opus: B13 appears on all 192 scored en pages as a general description of the method ('pulls a country's score toward...'). It does not claim that this particular country has thin data. Methodology boilerplate is accepted unless factually wrong or broken. The lowercase break after it is already covered by #15.

findings.quote: 8.0 homicides per 100,000 people (World Bank, 2022)
findings.problem: The 'main concern' sentence, which opens 'as of October 15, 2026', rests on a 2022 World Bank figure (SYC). Other examples: ZAF 43.7 (2022), TTO 40.4 (2022), SVG 51.3 (2023). The year is labelled, so this is not hidden, but an October 2026 summary names a 2022 datapoint as the main concern.
findings.expected: Show the data year next to the 'as of' date and flag the crime indicator when it is more than two years old, or use a newer edition.
findings.verification: opus: SYC really does say '8.0 homicides per 100,000 people (World Bank, 2022)', and latest.json has wb_homicide year 2022, which is the latest World Bank edition. The year is shown and homicide rates change slowly. This is not stale data passed off as current, which was the blogger's complaint.

findings.quote: The score is an uncertainty-weighted (Bayesian shrinkage) geometric mean of five pillars
findings.problem: Jargon a traveller cannot act on. This is FAQ sentence [B2], shown on 192 pages. A plain-language version, such as 'a weighted average that gives less weight to uncertain data', would still name the five pillars and avoid a sentence that sounds informative but says little.
findings.expected: A plain-language rewrite of B2 that still lists the five pillars and their weights.
findings.verification: opus: B2 is methodology boilerplate describing the formula. It is accurate (weights 30/25/20/15/10 match the formula) and not broken, so it falls under the accepted items. The jargon is a stylistic preference.

findings.quote: Come si confronta la sicurezza in Aruba con quella dei paesi confinanti e vicini?
findings.problem: Grey pages (no score and, by site rule, no comparison table) still carry a comparison heading in the batch: ABW, AIA, ALA, CXR, CCK and others. CCK and CXR say 'Nessuna fonte indipendente copre ancora questa destinazione' yet still promise a comparison. 'Paesi confinanti' (bordering countries) is wrong for islands with no land border (Aruba, Isole Cocos, Isola di Natale). Verify on the rendered page: if the heading shows without a table, it is a dangling heading.
findings.expected: No comparison heading on grey pages; for islands use 'paesi vicini' or name the real neighbours.
findings.verification: owner correction 2026-10-15: By design, not a defect: a grey (partial-data) place keeps its neighbour comparison table, with its own row shown as 'Partial data' next to scored neighbours (src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows). The audit brief wrongly listed 'no comparison table' among the accepted grey-page traits, and the verifier confirmed against that brief. Verifier had said: The finding's premise is wrong: there is no dangling heading. Grey pages render a full comparison table, with the subject row 'Dati parziali | – ...' and scored neighbours (ABW: Grenada/Rep. Dominicana/Venezuela/Haiti; CCK: Singapore/Malesia). ComparisonTable.astro deliberately keeps it for grey subjects. That still contradicts the stated grey rule (no comparison table). The heading 'paesi confinanti e vicini' is also used for islands with no land border (ABW, CCK, CXR, GGY), and CXR/CCK list Singapore/Malaysia but not Australia, the sovereign state.

findings.quote: Gli avvisi di viaggio di 17 governi dati sui conflitti UCDP Banca Mondiale
findings.problem: The source chips run together without separators, and 'dati sui conflitti UCDP' starts in lowercase, so it reads as 'governi dati sui conflitti'. Same on ESH: 'Gli avvisi di viaggio di 2 governi dati sui conflitti UCDP'.
findings.expected: Separate the chips with clear labels, each capitalised.
findings.verification: opus: ScoreHero.astro renders these items as a bulleted <ul>/<li> list, one source per line. The run-together text is an artefact of extracting the page as plain text. A lowercase bullet such as 'dati sui conflitti UCDP' is acceptable Italian.

findings.quote: La principale criticità è la criminalità violenta: 10,7 omicidi ogni 100.000 abitanti (Banca Mondiale, 2023)
findings.problem: The year is labelled, so this is not shown as current. But the headline main risk on a page dated 15 ottobre 2026 rests on a 2023 homicide rate. Same on BHS ('Banca Mondiale, 2022', 32,2) and BLZ ('Banca Mondiale, 2022', 28,1); CRI, DMA and ECU use 2023.
findings.expected: Caveat the vintage in the headline sentence, or use the latest vintage the source has.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on the ATG page, but the vintage is explicitly labelled ('Banca Mondiale, 2023'). latest.json shows these are the newest World Bank homicide years available (ATG 2023, BHS and BLZ 2022), and the WB series normally lags by 2-3 years. The data is labelled and is the latest vintage the source has, so it is not stale data presented as current.

findings.quote: Come si confronta la sicurezza in Guadalupa con quella dei paesi confinanti e vicini?
findings.problem: All 18 partial-data pages in the batch (GLP, MCO, JEY, MNP, MSR, MTQ, MYT, NFK, NIU, MAC, MAF, GRL, GUF, GUM, HKG, IMN, IOT, NCL) print a comparison heading ('Come si confronta la sicurezza in X con quella dei paesi confinanti e vicini?') with nothing under it. The accepted rule covers the missing comparison table on grey pages, but a heading that promises a neighbour comparison with no content is the 'comparison with no real neighbours' pattern the blogger complained about.
findings.expected: Hide the comparison heading on no-score pages, or show the neighbour list that actually exists. Keep the heading only where the table renders.
findings.verification: opus: The full page texts show the comparison heading followed by a real table on grey pages. IMN lists Irlanda and Belgio, GLP lists Antigua e Barbuda, Dominica and Saint Kitts e Nevis, and MCO and HKG also have rows. The claim that nothing appears under the heading is false.

findings.quote: invece di essere stimati a caso
findings.problem: Boilerplate read once. [B1] 'stimati a caso' says the estimates are random, but the method shrinks them toward a regional prior; 'calcolati con prudenza' fits better. [B8] 'lo pubblichiamo solo quando almeno quattro fonti indipendenti coprono un luogo, e qui sono meno' leaves 'meno' without a referent (meno di quattro). [B13] 'morti per conflitto (UCDP)' and 'pacificità complessiva' are awkward signal names ('morti in conflitti armati', 'livello di pace'). [B4] 'un consenso calibrato degli avvisi' is jargon. [B2] keeps 'Bayesian shrinkage' in English.
findings.expected: Fix the five phrases above. The formula description itself is otherwise acceptable.
findings.verification: opus: B1, B4, B8 and B13 exist as quoted, but they are understandable, grammatical Italian: 'invece di essere stimati a caso' means 'instead of being guessed', and 'qui sono meno' clearly refers to four sources. The 'Bayesian shrinkage' term is already covered in #17. These are stylistic preferences on accepted methodology boilerplate.

findings.quote: La principale criticità è la criminalità violenta: 8,0 omicidi ogni 100.000 abitanti (Banca Mondiale, 2022)
findings.problem: SYC, TTO, ZAF and VCT make a 2022 or 2023 World Bank homicide rate the headline risk of a page stamped 'Ultimo aggiornamento: 15 ottobre 2026'. TTO: '40,4 omicidi ogni 100.000 abitanti (Banca Mondiale, 2022)'; ZAF: 'Il rischio principale è la criminalità violenta: 43,7 omicidi ... (Banca Mondiale, 2022)'; VCT: '51,3 omicidi ... (Banca Mondiale, 2023)'. The year is printed, but nothing says the figure is three or four years old.
findings.expected: Flag the figure as the latest available year (for example 'dato 2022, ultimo disponibile') or base the headline risk on a current indicator.
findings.verification: opus: The SYC, TTO, ZAF and VCT summaries print the data year explicitly ('Banca Mondiale, 2022' / '2023'), so the figure is not presented as current. World Bank/UNODC homicide rates normally lag 2-3 years and these are the latest available. Adding 'ultimo disponibile' would be a nice touch, not a fix for misleading content.

findings.quote: Come si confronta la sicurezza in Porto Rico con quella dei paesi confinanti e vicini?
findings.problem: 13 partial-data pages (no score, and by the site's own rule no comparison table) still carry a comparison heading asking how safety compares with neighbours: PRI, REU, SJM, SMR, SXM, TCA, TKL, UMI, VAT, VGB, VIR, WLF, XKX. PCN, PYF, SGS, SHN and SPM have no such heading, so the grey pages are inconsistent with each other.
findings.expected: Remove the comparison heading from all grey pages, as PCN, SGS and SPM already do.
findings.verification: owner correction 2026-10-15: By design, not a defect: a grey (partial-data) place keeps its neighbour comparison table, with its own row shown as 'Partial data' next to scored neighbours (src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows). The audit brief wrongly listed 'no comparison table' among the accepted grey-page traits, and the verifier confirmed against that brief. Verifier had said: On partial-data pages, PRI.it has a full COMPARISON TABLE (a 'Porto Rico | Dati parziali' row plus Antigua, Dominica and the Dominican Republic), and UMI and XKX also carry comparison tables. PCN, SGS and SPM have none. This breaks the stated rule that grey pages have no comparison table, and the grey pages are inconsistent with each other.

findings.quote: (1/30 voti, 0/3 paesi di provenienza)
findings.problem: The community line reports 1 vote from 0 countries of origin. A vote should carry at least one origin country, so the counter reads as contradictory. It may be a vote without a country code, but the page does not say so.
findings.expected: Count the vote in the country tally, or show it as 'paese non indicato'.
findings.verification: opus: The text is on TUN.it, and latest.json has TUN community votes=1, origins=0. By design, origins counts only distinct known countries (src/pipeline/types.ts: 'the unknown group is not counted'), so 0/3 correctly shows progress toward the 3-origin threshold. It is not a contradiction.

findings.quote: Sentiment della community Community Non ci sono ancora abbastanza voti
findings.problem: On all 82 pages the community block repeats the word: 'Sentiment della community' is followed at once by the label 'Community'.
findings.expected: Keep one label, for example 'Sentiment della community' followed by 'Non ci sono ancora abbastanza voti'.
findings.verification: opus: 'Community' is not repeated text. It is a separate pill badge (t('sentiment.badge') in SentimentPillar.astro) next to the H2 'Sentiment della community', and the text extraction joins the two. It is an intentional UI tag, not broken Italian.

findings.quote: corretta per l'incertezza (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: An English technical term is left in parentheses in the boilerplate sentence B2, which is shown on 192 pages.
findings.expected: Translate it ('shrinkage bayesiano') or drop the parenthesis from the public text.
findings.verification: opus: B2 describes the formula and already gives the Italian gloss ('corretta per l'incertezza'). Keeping the technical name in parentheses is an accepted way to cite the method, and methodology boilerplate is accepted unless wrong or broken.

findings.quote: Come decidiamo quando pubblicare un punteggio→
findings.problem: On the 18 partial-data pages the HERO uses 'Cosa abbiamo' as a heading, which is unclear, and the link 'Come decidiamo quando pubblicare un punteggio→' ends with a stray arrow glyph that runs into the next label. Examples: PCN, PRI, UMI.
findings.expected: A clearer heading such as 'Dati disponibili', and a link without the stray glyph, or an arrow icon with proper spacing.
findings.verification: opus: The arrow is a deliberate link affordance (→ in ScoreHero.astro line 101), and it only runs into the next label in the flattened text. 'Cosa abbiamo' followed by the list of available sources is understandable Italian. The suggested change is a stylistic preference.

findings.quote: Rischio principale: rischi naturali (6.5).
findings.problem: The sentence 'Punteggio gratuito da 30+ fonti pubbliche, ricalcolato ogni giorno.' is missing from the DESCRIPTION on 12 pages (NZL, PNG, PRT, SAU, SLV, STP, SVK, SVN, SWE, TKM, TTO, VCT) while most scored pages have it, so the meta descriptions differ in form.
findings.expected: One DESCRIPTION template for all scored pages, fixed together with the 30+ source-count issue.
findings.verification: opus: This is intentional. src/lib/seo.ts sets DESCRIPTION_MAX=155 and drops the trailing sentence when the score and weakest-pillar text would exceed Google's display budget (e.g. NZL, PRT). The differing descriptions are by design, not an error.

findings.quote: Los 22 gobiernos que publican avisos para quien viaja a Afganistán desaconsejan todo viaje.
findings.problem: SUMMARY says all 22 governments advise against all travel, but FAQ Q3 on the same page says 'La mayoría de los gobiernos desaconsejan ya todo viaje' (a majority). This is the only page using this sentence; every other page gives the breakdown ('De los N gobiernos ... M desaconsejan todo viaje'), so the 22 figure is not supported by the page.
findings.expected: Use the standard breakdown with real counts, consistent with FAQ Q3.
findings.verification: opus: The AFG advisory list has 22 entries, all Nivel 4, so 'Los 22 gobiernos... desaconsejan todo viaje' is accurate. Q3's 'La mayoría' is weaker wording but not a contradiction.

findings.quote: El principal riesgo es el conflicto armado: 4333 personas murieron en conflictos armados en 2025 (UCDP).
findings.problem: Counts of 1000 or more lack the Spanish thousands separator (4333 on BFA, 8059 on COD, 5136 on ETH), while the site writes '100.000' with a dot elsewhere.
findings.verification: opus: '4333', '8059' and '5136' are on the pages, but RAE/CLDR Spanish style writes four-digit numbers without a separator and groups from five digits up. The site does exactly that: PSE '14.505', SDN '75.044', UKR '90.345'. The output is correct, not broken.

findings.quote: corrección por incertidumbre (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: Untranslated English in Spanish text: the methodology boilerplate B1 keeps '(Bayesian shrinkage)', and 'Global Peace Index' appears 32 times on 19 pages (SUMMARY, FAQ and B13/B18 text) where Spanish readers expect 'Índice Global de Paz'. INFORM, UCDP and V-Dem can stay as names.
findings.expected: '(contracción bayesiana)' or drop the parenthetical; 'Índice Global de Paz (GPI)' on first mention.
findings.verification: opus: B1 does contain '(Bayesian shrinkage)', but only as a parenthetical after the Spanish gloss 'corrección por incertidumbre', in intentional methodology boilerplate. 'Global Peace Index' is the proper name of the IEP publication, used in indicator tables like the other source names. Stylistic preference only.

findings.quote: ReliefWeb (solo mientras hay un desastre en curso, así que no cuenta entre las cuatro)
findings.problem: Internal method note leaks into the visitor-facing HERO: 'no cuenta entre las cuatro' refers to the four-source threshold, which the reader never sees. ReliefWeb is a humanitarian information service, listed in the same 'Lo que sí tenemos' block as the government advisories (ASM; COK has the same parenthetical).
findings.expected: Drop the parenthetical, or rewrite it for travellers (for example: ReliefWeb solo informa mientras dura una emergencia).
findings.verification: opus: The quote is in the ASM and COK HERO, but the same HERO states the threshold just before it ('Solo publicamos una puntuación ... cuando al menos cuatro fuentes independientes cubren un destino; para este tenemos menos de cuatro'), so 'no cuenta entre las cuatro' refers to something the reader does see. At most slightly awkward phrasing.

findings.field: FAQ A3 on no-score pages vs HERO
findings.quote: El panorama general es tranquilizador
findings.problem: 15 pages with no official score (GLP, GRL, GUF, GUM, IMN, IOT, JEY, MAC, MAF, MCO, MNP, MSR, MTQ, MYT, NIU) get the overall verdict 'El panorama general es tranquilizador' while the same page's HERO says 'Sin puntuación de seguridad oficial'. The grey-page advisory breakdown is not in the dump, so the 'ninguno lo sitúa…' part cannot be checked for these pages.
findings.expected: On no-score pages, describe the advisories and their count without a general 'tranquilizador' verdict.
findings.verification: opus: The 'tranquilizador' sentence is explicitly about the government advisories (e.g. GLP: 10 advisories, all normal precautions). The HERO also lists those advisories under 'Lo que sí tenemos', so it does not contradict 'Sin puntuación de seguridad oficial'. The n=1 wording problem is covered by #16.

findings.quote: ¿Cómo se compara Guadalupe con sus países vecinos y cercanos?
findings.problem: All 18 grey pages (GLP, GRL, GUF, GUM, HKG, IMN, IOT, JEY, MAC, MAF, MCO, MNP, MSR, MTQ, MYT, NCL, NFK, NIU) carry the comparison heading, and nothing follows it in the dump (no table, no text). The heading promises a comparison the page does not show.
findings.expected: Hide the heading when no comparison table renders, or replace it with one sentence explaining why there is no comparison.
findings.verification: opus: False claim. The comparison table does render under the heading on grey pages: GLP lists Antigua y Barbuda and Dominica, MCO lists Suiza and Italia, NFK lists Nueva Zelanda, HKG lists Taiwán, NIU lists Fiyi and IOT lists Sri Lanka.

findings.quote: La principal preocupación es la delincuencia violenta: 8,0 homicidios por cada 100.000 habitantes (Banco Mundial, 2022).
findings.problem: A 2022 or 2023 World Bank homicide figure is written in the present tense as the page's main concern on an October 2026 page: SYC 8,0 (2022), TTO 40,4 (2022), ZAF 43,7 (2022, 'El principal riesgo es...'), VCT 51,3 (2023). The year is printed, but 'es' presents the claim as current, the old-data-as-current pattern the blogger flagged.
findings.expected: Say 'último dato disponible (2022)' in the sentence, or stop ranking a figure older than about three years as the principal concern.
findings.verification: opus: The year is printed inline ('Banco Mundial, 2022'), the indicator table explains the World Bank's publication lag, and 2022/2023 are the latest WB homicide releases. It is not old data presented as current.

findings.quote: ¿Cómo se compara Puerto Rico con sus países vecinos y cercanos?
findings.problem: 13 no-score pages (PRI, REU, SJM, SMR, SXM, TCA, TKL, UMI, VAT, VGB, VIR, WLF, XKX) still carry a COMPARISON HEADING question ('¿Cómo se compara X con sus países vecinos...?'), although the accepted design gives these places no comparison table. If the heading renders, it is a question over an empty section, the same neighbours-comparison pattern the blogger attacked. Verify in the template.
findings.expected: Do not emit the comparison heading on no-score pages.
findings.verification: opus: The heading is not over an empty section. On all 13 pages (e.g. PRI, REU, XKX) it sits above a filled table: the place shows 'Datos parciales' and 2-4 scored neighbours or nearby places. src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows() deliberately puts a grey subject first with no numbers, so this is by design. Separate real issue: SJM's table lists Islandia/Finlandia/Suecia but not Norway, because NOR's coordinates (Oslo) are beyond the 2000 km nearby cap.

findings.quote: V-Dem puntúa la imparcialidad de la administración pública con 0,30 en una escala de −4 a +4 aprox., donde más alto es mejor
findings.problem: A 0,30 on a roughly −4 to +4 scale sits near the middle, yet it is presented as the 'punto más débil ... poco imparcial'. 'aprox.' inside a data statement is vague.
findings.expected: State the position plainly ('valor cercano al centro de la escala') and avoid 'poco imparcial' unless the scale supports it.
findings.verification: opus: The quote exists, but the claim is wrong. On V-Dem's latent scale, SVK's 0,30 is genuinely low for Europe (DEU 3,99, CZE 3,24, AUT 2,15, POL 1,33, close to HUN 0,26), so 'poco imparcial' is defensible. 'aprox.' honestly describes the open latent scale. A peer reference point would help, but nothing on the page is wrong.

findings.quote: Gobernanza 5.4/10 * Cuando un pilar tiene poca cobertura de datos, su contribución a la puntuación general se reduce o se excluye.
findings.problem: On NRU, PLW, TON, TUV, TWN and WSM the same explanation is printed twice inside one bar list, after each low-coverage pillar, which breaks the list. Other pages show it once.
findings.expected: Show the note once below the bar list.
findings.verification: opus: This is an extraction artifact. PillarBreakdown.astro renders a '*' button for each low-coverage pillar, and PillarCoverageTip shows the note only in a hidden tooltip (invisible until hover/focus). The visible list does not repeat the sentence.

findings.quote: así que no cuenta entre las cuatro
findings.problem: On REU and TCA the HERO says ReliefWeb is only counted 'mientras hay un desastre en curso, así que no cuenta entre las cuatro'. 'Las cuatro' refers to the four-source threshold, which the reader never sees defined on that line.
findings.expected: '... no cuenta para el mínimo de cuatro fuentes independientes'.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on REU and TCA, but the four-source threshold is defined in the same HERO just above ('al menos cuatro fuentes independientes... tenemos menos de cuatro'), so the reader does see what 'las cuatro' refers to. This is a mere stylistic preference.

findings.quote: Comment la sécurité en Aruba se compare-t-elle à celle des pays voisins et proches ?
findings.problem: The batch carries a comparison heading ('se compare-t-elle à celle des pays voisins et proches') on 16 partial-data pages (ABW, AIA, ALA, AND, ASM, BES, BLM, CCK, COK, CUW, CXR, CYM, ESH, FRO, GGY, GIB). Per the accepted design these pages have no comparison table, so if the heading renders it promises a neighbours comparison with nothing beneath it, which is the blogger's 'compare with neighbours' complaint in another form. The batch shows headings, not the rendered section, so confirm on the live pages.
findings.expected: Suppress the comparison heading whenever the comparison table is suppressed, or show a one-line explanation in its place.
findings.verification: opus: The claim that the heading has nothing beneath it is wrong. The page files for ESH, CCK and GGY show the comparison heading followed by real rows (e.g. GGY: Irlande, Belgique, Royaume-Uni, France marked 'proche'; CCK: Singapour, Malaisie). The partial place appears greyed in the table, so there is no empty heading. Note for the orchestrator: partial pages do render a neighbour table, contrary to the accepted-design note.

findings.quote: Consultez les avis disponibles et notez votre voyage.
findings.problem: On the 20 partial-data pages, 'notez votre voyage' ('rate your trip') is an awkward calque. The community vote asks how safe the traveller felt, not to rate a trip.
findings.expected: 'Consultez les avis disponibles et partagez votre ressenti.'
findings.verification: opus: 'Consultez les avis disponibles et notez votre voyage' is on ABW and is idiomatic, understandable French. Calling it off-target is a stylistic preference.

findings.quote: Le principal risque est la criminalité violente : 32,2 homicides pour 100 000 habitants (Banque mondiale, 2022).
findings.problem: The 'principal risque' of a page dated 15 octobre 2026 rests on a 2022 homicide rate. The year is labelled, so no date is false, but the headline risk is presented as current. The same pattern uses 2023 figures on CRI, ECU, DMA and ATG; BLZ uses 2022.
findings.expected: State the year as context in the sentence and check the main-risk ranking against the latest available year, or flag when the main-risk figure is older than the score it accompanies.
findings.verification: opus: The BHS SUMMARY labels the year ('Banque mondiale, 2022'), and the indicator table explains the World Bank's 1–2 year publication lag. 2022 is the latest WB value used. The page labels the figure's age instead of presenting it as current, so this is not the stale-data problem the blogger described.

findings.quote: Côté points forts, le pilier risques naturels arrive en tête, à 6.3/10.
findings.problem: 'Côté points forts, le pilier X arrive en tête' is a calque of the English 'on the strengths side'. It comes from boilerplate [B6], [B17] and [B21] and from plain-text variants. A French editor writes 'Point fort : …' or 'Le domaine le mieux noté est …'. 'Les signaux les moins bien notés' is also a stiff calque.
findings.expected: 'Point fort : le pilier risques naturels (6.3/10), le mieux noté.'
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on CMR. 'Côté points forts, … arrive en tête' is ordinary idiomatic French (the 'côté X' construction is common), and so is 'les moins bien notés'. This is a stylistic preference, not broken text.

findings.quote: Pays similaires > Dans la même région
findings.problem: The '>' glyph inside a heading (63 pages) reads like a breadcrumb separator. It is not French typography, and the heading reads as a path rather than a subsection.
findings.expected: A sub-heading, or 'Pays similaires : dans la même région'.
findings.verification: opus: The '>' is not on the page. scripts/audit/extract-page-facts.ts joins the h2 'Pays similaires' and the h3 'Dans la même région' when it builds the RELATED line; RelatedCountries.astro renders them as separate headings.

findings.quote: Sentiment de la communauté Communauté
findings.problem: Doubled label: 'communauté' appears twice in the community heading on every page (103 occurrences across the COMMUNITY and HERO fields of the batch).
findings.expected: Drop the second label, or give it its own heading style.
findings.verification: opus: This is the h2 'Sentiment de la communauté' (country.pillar.sentiment) followed by a separate badge pill 'Communauté' (sentiment.badge in SentimentPillar.astro), joined by the text extraction. It is a styled badge, not a doubled word in the heading.

findings.quote: aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau
findings.problem: The template 'Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant : la plupart des gouvernements ne recommandent que des précautions normales ..., et aucun ne le place au-dessus d'un avis de faible niveau' is also used on 22 score pages whose SUMMARY reports governments recommending 'une vigilance renforcée', which is above normal precautions: GRC (2 of 21), GRD (6 of 19), KAZ (9 of 20), NAM (6 of 20), NLD (6 of 20), MNG (7 of 19), ISL (2 of 19), LUX (1 of 20), IRL (1 of 18), KNA (1 of 15; the same page's SUMMARY names 'la criminalité violente : 64,2 homicides' as the principal risk). The sentence is false whenever one government advises increased caution.
findings.expected: Generate the sentence from the counts (for example 'X gouvernements sur N recommandent les précautions habituelles et Y une vigilance renforcée'). Use 'rassurant' only when no government is above normal precautions, and never beside a main-risk statement the page itself makes.
findings.verification: opus: The sentence is on the pages, but 'un avis de faible niveau' naturally includes level 2 (increased caution). In every case listed, a majority recommends normal precautions and nobody goes above level 2 (e.g. GRC 19/2, KAZ 11/9, KNA 14/1), so the sentence is true.

findings.quote: Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant
findings.problem: Fifteen partial-data pages (GLP, GRL, GUF, GUM, IMN, IOT, JEY, MAC, MAF, MCO, MNP, MSR, MTQ, MYT, NIU) say they have no official score (TITLE 'Données partielles', HERO 'Pas de score de sécurité officiel') and then describe the advisories as 'Le tableau d'ensemble est rassurant'. That is a reassuring safety verdict without a score, on pages designed to show none. Examples: GLP (10 advisories), MAF (4), IOT (1).
findings.expected: On partial-data pages describe the advisories neutrally, for example 'X gouvernements ont publié un avis ; ces avis ne constituent pas un score de sécurité.' Drop 'rassurant' there.
findings.verification: opus: On GLP, MAF and IOT the sentence describes the advisories only and gives no score. Calling level-1 advisories reassuring does not break the grey/partial-data design, which is accepted. The N=1 wording problem is covered by #11.

findings.quote: Comment la sécurité en Guadeloupe se compare-t-elle à celle des pays voisins et proches ?
findings.problem: Partial-data pages, which the design says have no comparison table, still carry a COMPARISON HEADING question with no RELATED lines or comparison data in the file: GLP, GRL, GUF, GUM, HKG, IMN, IOT, JEY, MAC, MAF, MCO, MNP, MSR, MTQ, MYT, NCL, NFK, NIU. If the heading renders, the page asks a comparison question it does not answer.
findings.expected: Omit the heading on partial-data pages, or state briefly why no comparison is shown yet.
findings.verification: opus: The batch extractor lists no table rows for any page, scored pages included. In the built HTML (dist/client/fr/pays/glp and nfk), the table is rendered with the place marked 'Données partielles' and real nearby rows (Antigua-et-Barbuda, Dominique; Nouvelle-Zélande, Fidji), so the heading is answered.

findings.quote: O principal risco é a criminalidade violenta: 32,2 homicídios por 100 mil habitantes (Banco Mundial, 2022).
findings.problem: The present-tense 'O principal risco é' rests on a World Bank homicide rate from 2022 (BHS, BLZ) or 2023 (ATG, CRI, DMA, ECU) on pages dated 15 October 2026. The year is printed, but the figure is still presented as the current main risk. ATG uses the same pattern ('A principal preocupação é a criminalidade violenta: 10,7 homicídios ... (Banco Mundial, 2023)').
findings.expected: Past tense with the year ('Em 2022, a taxa foi de 32,2...') and a note that it is the latest available value, or base the 'principal risco' on a current indicator.
findings.verification: opus: The year of the World Bank homicide figure is printed explicitly (2022/2023), and it is the latest release of a slow-moving annual series. Calling crime the main risk is a fair present-tense conclusion. This is not data presented as current without a date.

findings.quote: COMPARISON HEADING: Como se compara a segurança de Aruba com a dos países vizinhos e próximos?
findings.problem: 16 of the 20 grey pages carry this heading, although grey pages have no score, no rank and no comparison table by design. Cocos (CCK), whose HERO says 'Nenhuma fonte independente cobre este destino ainda', still promises a comparison with 'países vizinhos e próximos'. This is the empty 'neighbours' comparison the blogger criticised. The heading is listed as page text in the batch; whether it renders without a table was not verified.
findings.expected: Hide the heading on grey pages, or replace it with one line saying no comparison is shown because the data are insufficient.
findings.verification: opus: The premise is wrong. Grey pages render a real comparison table under the heading: the grey place shows 'Dados parciais' and nearby scored countries follow (CCK: Singapura, Malásia; GGY: Irlanda, Bélgica, Reino Unido, França; ALA: Finlândia, Estônia...). The heading is not empty.

findings.quote: É seguro viajar para o Barein? 6.6/10 (2026)
findings.problem: 'Barein' is not the usual pt-BR spelling (Bahrein; pt-PT uses Barém). It repeats in H1, DESCRIPTION, HERO, SUMMARY and FAQ.
findings.expected: 'Bahrein' throughout, matching the site's pt-BR register.
findings.verification: opus: 'Barein' appears 14 times on BHR.pt, but it is a recognised Portuguese spelling, alongside Bahrein and Barém, and Brazilian sources use it. Preferring 'Bahrein' is a style choice, not an error.

findings.quote: 4.333 pessoas morreram em conflitos armados em 2025 (UCDP)
findings.problem: A dot as thousands separator is correct pt-BR, but this site uses the dot as the decimal mark in scores ('7.3/10'), so '4.333' can be read as 4.3. COD ('8.059 pessoas') and ETH ('5.136 pessoas') have the same issue.
findings.expected: A space as thousands separator ('4 333 pessoas'), or a rounded figure in words ('cerca de 4,3 mil').
findings.verification: opus: '4.333 pessoas', '8.059' and '5.136' use the correct Portuguese thousands separator. A count of people can't be read as a decimal, and the dot-decimal in scores is an accepted convention.

findings.quote: (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: English term left inside the Portuguese methodology FAQ (boilerplate B1, shown on 192 pages).
findings.expected: Portuguese wording (for example 'encolhimento bayesiano') or remove the English.
findings.verification: opus: B1 reads 'média geométrica ponderada com correção de incerteza (Bayesian shrinkage)'. The Portuguese wording is already there; the English term is only a technical gloss in parentheses, which is common in Portuguese technical writing. This is intentional methodology text and a style preference at most.

findings.quote: Como se compara a segurança da Ilha Norfolk com a dos países vizinhos e próximos?
findings.problem: All 18 partial-data pages carry a heading promising a comparison with 'países vizinhos e próximos', and the batch shows no table or content under it. The accepted rule says partial pages have no comparison table. For NFK the page says 'Nenhuma fonte independente cobre este destino ainda', so there is nothing to compare. The same heading appears on GLP and GRL.
findings.expected: Remove the comparison heading on partial-data pages, or replace it with a line saying no comparison is shown. Confirm on the rendered page whether the heading is visible.
findings.verification: opus: The claim that there is no content under the heading is wrong. NFK.pt (and GLP, GRL) render a real COMPARISON TABLE with Nova Zelândia, Fiji, Tonga and Vanuatu marked 'próximo', plus a 'Dados parciais' row of dashes for NFK. The heading is accurate. Whether partial pages should show the table at all is a separate design question, not this finding.

findings.quote: com correção de incerteza (Bayesian shrinkage)
findings.problem: Untranslated English term inside methodology boilerplate B1, which appears on the scored pages' score paragraph (B1 is on 192 pages site-wide).
findings.expected: Translate it (e.g. 'com ajuste bayesiano') or drop the parenthesis.
findings.verification: opus: B1 does contain 'correção de incerteza (Bayesian shrinkage)', but this is the pt term followed by the English technical gloss in parentheses. That is intentional methodology boilerplate, neither broken nor wrong, so changing it is a stylistic preference.

findings.quote: Criminalidade 5.7/10 * Quando um pilar tem pouca cobertura de dados
findings.problem: On pages with low-coverage pillars the explanatory note is pasted after each starred pillar inside the bar line. On KIR and MHL the same sentence appears twice in one line.
findings.expected: Show the note once below the bars, with a single asterisk marker per low-coverage pillar.
findings.verification: opus: The repeated sentence comes from PillarCoverageTip.astro, a '*' button with a hidden role=tooltip span (invisible until hover or focus). Visitors see one asterisk per pillar; only the text extraction pastes the hidden tooltip inline.

findings.quote: O principal risco é a criminalidade violenta: 51,3 homicídios por 100 mil habitantes (Banco Mundial, 2023).
findings.problem: VCT's headline risk rests on World Bank homicide data from 2023. SYC (8,0 homicides, 'Banco Mundial, 2022'), TTO and ZAF (both 2022) repeat the pattern. The year is printed, but the 'principal' claim is built on data three to four years old in a page dated 15 de outubro de 2026, and the homicide rate is one of the two inputs of the crime pillar (33%, per the project formula).
findings.expected: Use the newest World Bank homicide edition, or state the year clearly and do not present an old figure as the main concern.
findings.verification: opus: In latest.json the newest World Bank homicide year is 2023 (82 countries; none later), so VCT already uses the newest edition. The page prints the year and a note on the 1-2 year publication lag. This is labelled, not stale data shown as current.

findings.quote: O ponto mais fraco é a fragilidade da governança: 4,9 de 10 na escala do INFORM
findings.problem: The same page shows governança as 'Governança 5.9/10' in PILLAR BARS and 'governança, com 5.9/10' in FAQ Q2. The SUMMARY's 'weakest point' carries another number (4,9) without saying it is an INFORM sub-indicator on a 0-10 risk scale, so a reader sees two governance scores for the same area.
findings.expected: Quote the pillar score (5.9/10) for the pillar. If the INFORM value stays, label it as a sub-indicator with its direction (10 = worst).
findings.verification: opus: The ROU SUMMARY reads 'O ponto mais fraco é a fragilidade da governança: 4,9 de 10 na escala do INFORM, sendo 10 o pior', so it does name the INFORM scale and its direction, contrary to the finding. Governança 5.9/10 is also the lowest bar, so the 'weakest point' agrees with the pillars.

findings.quote: Como se compara a segurança das Ilhas Menores Distantes dos Estados Unidos com a dos países vizinhos e próximos?
findings.problem: 13 of the 18 no-score pages keep the comparison heading 'Como se compara a segurança de X com a dos países vizinhos e próximos?' (examples UMI, VAT and SMR; also PRI, REU, SJM, SXM, TCA, TKL, VGB, VIR, WLF, XKX). Under the accepted design these pages have no score, rank or comparison, so the heading promises a comparison the page cannot make. UMI says 'Nenhuma fonte independente cobre este destino ainda' and has no real neighbours: the blogger's neighbours complaint in a new place.
findings.expected: Drop the comparison heading on partial-data pages, or replace it with a line saying that no comparison is shown without a score.
findings.verification: owner correction 2026-10-15: By design, not a defect: a grey (partial-data) place keeps its neighbour comparison table, with its own row shown as 'Partial data' next to scored neighbours (src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows). The audit brief wrongly listed 'no comparison table' among the accepted grey-page traits, and the verifier confirmed against that brief. Verifier had said: UMI, VAT and SMR (partial data) render not just the heading but a full neighbour comparison table (UMI: Ilhas Marshall, Micronésia; VAT: Eslovênia, Croácia ahead of Itália). The accepted design says partial-data places get no comparison table, so the table itself should not be shown. VAT also lists distant 'próximo' countries ahead of its only real neighbour.

findings.quote: em vez de ser estimada ao acaso
findings.problem: B4 'estimada ao acaso' (estimated at random) says the opposite of what is meant: the score is pulled toward a regional prior, not guessed at random. B1 leaves the English '(Bayesian shrinkage)' in pt text, and B2's 'um consenso calibrado dos avisos' is jargon a traveller cannot parse. All three boilerplate lines appear on 192 pages.
findings.expected: For example 'em vez de ser estimada sem base' / 'correção bayesiana (encolhimento estatístico)' / 'um consenso ponderado dos avisos de viagem'.
findings.verification: opus: B1, B2 and B4 are on the batch's boilerplate list as quoted. 'Em vez de ser estimada ao acaso' means 'rather than guessed at random', which matches the English intent; it is not the opposite. The '(Bayesian shrinkage)' gloss is kept on purpose in every language, and 'consenso calibrado' is acceptable pt. This is intentional methodology boilerplate and a matter of style.

findings.quote: Os alertas de viagem de 5 governos ReliefWeb (apenas enquanto há um desastre em curso, por isso não conta entre as quatro)
findings.problem: The source list reads as if ReliefWeb were a government ('5 governos ReliefWeb'), and the parenthesis is hard to follow ('por isso não conta entre as quatro'). The same pattern appears on TCA ('8 governos ReliefWeb').
findings.expected: Separate the sources, e.g. 'Alertas de 5 governos e ReliefWeb (só durante desastres em curso; não entra na contagem das quatro fontes)'.
findings.verification: opus: The text appears on ASM/COK/NCL/REU/TCA as 'Os alertas de viagem de 8 governos ReliefWeb (…)' only because the extraction joins separate list items: grey-copy.ts renders the advisories label and the ReliefWeb alertItem as distinct entries in the 'O que temos' list. On the rendered page ReliefWeb is not shown as a government, and 'não conta entre as quatro' makes sense next to the 'pelo menos quatro fontes' sentence just before it.

findings.quote: 最需关注：健康（6.6分）。
findings.problem: On 36 of 62 scored pages the headline 'most concern' pillar is not the lowest pillar shown without a low-coverage footnote. AZE: PILLAR BARS shows 治理 2.9/10, 3.7 points below the headlined health (6.6). SUMMARY headlines '最需关注的是流行病传播：INFORM评分为4.2/10', and the FAQ then calls governance the '尤其是' weak pillar (治理（2.9/10）). BDI (conflict 5.5 headlined, governance 2.5) and BOL (health 5.2 headlined, governance 3.8) show the same split. Cause: src/lib/country-summary.ts selectDriverPillar (about line 163) considers only DIRECT_RISK_PILLARS while any of them is under 7.0, so governance can be the headline only when every direct-risk pillar is 7+. The headline therefore understates the weakest pillar and the page contradicts itself.
findings.expected: Headline the lowest pillar when it is far below the driver, or state in SUMMARY and DESCRIPTION that governance is the weakest pillar even though it is not counted as a direct risk.
findings.verification: opus: This is deliberate v10 design. selectDriverPillar (country-summary.ts) headlines the direct-risk pillar that drags the score most, not governance; it was the fix for the blogger's 'biggest concern is governance' complaint (its docstring cites Ecuador crime 4.4 over governance 4.0). The remaining clash with the FAQ's weakest-pillar wording is covered by #2 and #4.

findings.quote: 为阿富汗发布旅行警告的22个国家政府均建议避免一切旅行。
findings.problem: SUMMARY says all 22 governments advise avoiding all travel. The FAQ on the same page says '多数政府目前建议完全避免前往阿富汗' (most governments). 'All' and 'most' cannot both be right, and no breakdown is given to settle it.
findings.expected: Give the real count (e.g. '19 of 22 governments advise avoiding all travel') and keep the FAQ wording consistent with it.
findings.verification: opus: All 22 AFG advisory cards are level 4, so the SUMMARY's 'all 22' is correct. The FAQ's 多数 (most) is weaker but not contradictory: all implies most. The proposed '19 of 22' is invented.

findings.quote: 阿鲁巴 与邻国及附近国家相比如何？
findings.problem: The accepted rule says grey places show no comparison table, but 16 grey pages (ABW, AIA, ALA, AND, ASM, BES, BLM, CCK, COK, CUW, CXR, CYM, ESH, FRO, GGY, GIB) render this heading. ComparisonTable.astro is included on every country page (src/components/country/CountryPageBody.astro line 136, not gated on scored) and renders its block only when the rows (country plus neighbours plus nearby fillers) exceed one. The heading sits in the same block, so a neighbour table with scores is probably rendered beside a blank row for the grey place. Not checked on the live DOM. This is the 'compare with neighbours' pattern the blogger objected to.
findings.expected: Hide the comparison block for grey places (RelatedCountries already withholds for the data floor), or confirm on the live page and show a 'not scored' note instead of a neighbour ranking.
findings.verification: owner correction 2026-10-15: By design, not a defect: a grey (partial-data) place keeps its neighbour comparison table, with its own row shown as 'Partial data' next to scored neighbours (src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows). The audit brief wrongly listed 'no comparison table' among the accepted grey-page traits, and the verifier confirmed against that brief. Verifier had said: Grey pages ABW, GGY and ALA all render a comparison table with the grey place as '数据不完整' next to scored neighbours. This contradicts the stated intent that grey places get no comparison table. The 'nearby' fillers are also loose (Haiti and Venezuela for Aruba; Belgium and Ireland for Guernsey).

findings.quote: 主要风险是暴力犯罪：每10万人中有32.2起故意杀人案（世界银行，2022年）。
findings.problem: Dated 2026-10-15, but the headline risk uses a 2022 World Bank figure (BHS, BLZ) or a 2023 figure (ATG, CRI, DMA, ECU). The year is printed, so the date is not hidden, but the headline rests on a 3-4-year-old indicator next to a current score.
findings.expected: Print the data year next to the headline figure and flag that it is older than the score, or use a current source.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on BHS (and similar text with 2023 is on CRI/ECU), but the data year is printed next to the figure. World Bank homicide data normally lags 2-3 years, so this is the latest release, properly labelled, and not stale data presented as current.

findings.quote: 是的——保加利亚是我们指数中最安全的目的地之一
findings.problem: The superlative attaches to the 'risk very low' score band (8.0+), not to rank. SUMMARY gives rank 39 of 192, which is the top fifth rather than 'one of the safest'. FRA (rank 37) has the same claim.
findings.expected: Tie the claim to rank (e.g. 'top fifth of the 192 scored places') or to the band (e.g. 'in the lowest-risk band').
findings.verification: opus: BGR is rank 39/192 with 8.0 and FRA is rank 37 with 8.1, both in the top band, which is roughly the top 20% of scored places. Calling them 'one of the safest destinations in our index' is defensible for a top-band, top-fifth place and not misleading.

findings.quote: 即使是其最薄弱的领域自然灾害也得到了 7.8/10 的分数，稳居低风险区间
findings.problem: 得到了…的分数 (received a score of) is a machine-translated construction repeated in FAQ 2 on 8 pages (IRL, ISL, LTU, LUX, LVA, MHL, MLT, NOR). A native would write 最弱的自然灾害也有7.8/10，仍属低风险.
findings.expected: Plain wording, e.g. 即使最弱的自然灾害也有7.8/10，仍处于低风险区间.
findings.verification: opus: The quote exists (CHE, IRL, LVA; the same template is on ~27 pages), but 即使是其最薄弱的领域X也得到了 7.8/10 的分数，稳居低风险区间 is grammatical, natural Chinese. The suggested rewrite is a stylistic preference.

findings.quote: 表现最好的方面是健康（8.7/10）。
findings.problem: The best area names one pillar when another pillar has the same score: HRV conflict 8.7 = health 8.7. Similar ties on GRC (conflict 8.3 = health 8.3), KWT (health 7.0 = crime 7.0) and KEN (crime 6.1 = natural hazards 6.1, where the FAQ names crime). The page does not say it is a tie, so the strongest label is an arbitrary tie-break.
findings.expected: Say tied or name both pillars.
findings.verification: opus: The ties exist only after rounding to one decimal. In latest.json HRV health 0.8689 > conflict 0.8664, GRC conflict 0.8297 > health 0.8293, and KWT health 0.7029 > crime 0.6979, so the named best pillar is correct, not an arbitrary tie-break. KEN's SUMMARY names no best pillar.

findings.quote: 最需关注的是暴力犯罪：每10万人中有5.1起故意杀人案（世界银行，2021年）。
findings.problem: The main concern rests on a 2021 homicide figure, while the same indicator is 2023 elsewhere (GRD: 世界银行，2023年) and LUX's lowest-pillar sentence uses 2022. The year is labelled, but a five-year-old value is presented as the current main concern, and 5.1 per 100,000 is a low rate to name as the top concern.
findings.expected: Use the latest year available for this indicator or flag the figure as old; re-check the main concern against current data.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is exact. 2021 is the latest wb_homicide year in latest.json for LIE, and the indicator table flags the World Bank lag, so it is labelled and not shown as current. 5.1/100k is high for Western Europe and matches crime (6.6) being the lowest pillar bar. A possible real issue is that it is a small-population noise figure (a handful of cases) driving the 'main concern', but that is a different claim from the stale-data one made here.

findings.quote: 最需关注的是暴力犯罪：每10万人中有8.0起故意杀人案（世界银行，2022年）。
findings.problem: The headline concern on SYC, TTO and ZAF rests on World Bank homicide data labelled 2022 (VCT uses 2023). The SUMMARY opens 截至2026年10月15日 and presents the figure as the current top concern. The year label is there, but the headline is built on a value three to four years old with no staleness note.
findings.expected: Put the data year and a staleness note next to the headline figure, or lead with a current indicator where one exists, such as the GPI safety score used elsewhere on the same pages.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on SYC (TTO and ZAF are similar), but the year (世界银行，2022年) sits right next to the figure, and 2022 is a normal World Bank WDI release lag. The data is not passed off as current.

findings.quote: 美国本土外小岛屿 与邻国及附近国家相比如何？
findings.problem: Unscored (grey) pages carry a compare-with-neighbours heading with no rows in the batch: UMI, VAT, VGB, VIR, WLF, XKX, TKL, TCA, SXM, SMR, SJM, REU, PRI (13 pages). PCN, PYF, SGS, SHN and SPM have none. The site rule says grey pages have no comparison table, so the heading is an empty section, and its presence is inconsistent across grey pages.
findings.expected: Hide the comparison heading on every unscored page, or render the same block on all of them only after checking that it has rows.
findings.verification: opus: The claim that the heading has no rows is wrong. UMI, VAT and PRI have real rows: the grey place plus 2–4 scored nearby countries. The pages without the table (PCN, PYF, SGS, SHN, SPM, ATA, BVT, FLK, ATF) are remote places with no scored neighbours, so the difference is consistent and the section is not empty.

findings.quote: V-Dem对公共行政公正性的评分为0.30
findings.problem: The SUMMARY calls public-administration impartiality the weakest area and gives 0.30 on a scale described as about −4 to +4 (higher is better). On that scale 0.30 is near the midpoint, not a weakness. SRB states its V-Dem value on 0–1. Not checked against V-Dem itself; verify the scale and direction for this indicator.
findings.expected: State the scale actually used, confirm the value supports the label, and use one scale per indicator family.
findings.verification: opus: The SVK value 0.298 on the V-Dem latent scale (about −4 to +4, higher is better) matches the data. It normalises to 0.54, Slovakia's lowest governance indicator (others 0.71 and 0.73), so calling it the weakest area is correct. SRB's 0–1 value is a different indicator (political corruption), so the scales are not mixed.

findings.quote: 经不确定性加权（贝叶斯收缩）计算得出的几何平均数
findings.problem: B2 says the score is the geometric mean of the five pillars. The project's formula notes in CLAUDE.md (v9.1) also describe a soft-min term over conflict and crime, a severe-advisory modifier and a 1+9·x^0.96 rescale, which the sentence omits. The v10 formula was not available to check, so this may be a simplification rather than an error.
findings.expected: If the live formula has these steps, add one clause naming them; otherwise confirm that the sentence still holds.
findings.verification: opus: This is methodology boilerplate, which is accepted. B3, right after it, already covers the weak-pillar penalty and the calibrated advisory consensus, so the description is simplified but not wrong.

findings.quote: Das Gesamtbild ist beruhigend: Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen für Aruba nur normale Vorsicht
findings.problem: On 18 grey pages the site states there is no safety assessment ('Keine offizielle Sicherheitsbewertung', 'weniger als vier unabhängige Quellen'), yet the FAQ gives an overall reassuring verdict or a predominant recommendation. GIB: 'Das Gesamtbild ist beruhigend' with 4 governments. ESH: 'Die vorherrschende Empfehlung lautet, eine Reise nach Westsahara zu überdenken'. Same template on AIA, ALA, AND, ASM, ATA, ATF, BES, BLM, BVT, COK, CUW, CYM, FLK, FRO, GGY.
findings.expected: No verdict, 'beruhigend' or 'vorherrschende Empfehlung' on grey pages. List the advisories without judgement.
findings.verification: opus: On grey pages (GIB, ABW, ESH) the first FAQ gives no site verdict and tells readers to check the advisories. The second FAQ only summarises what the governments themselves say ('Das Gesamtbild ist beruhigend: Die meisten Regierungen empfehlen ... normale Vorsicht'). That is a factual description of the advisories, not a safety score, so it does not contradict 'keine offizielle Sicherheitsbewertung'. The wrong quantifier with n=1 is covered separately in #11.

findings.quote: Für Deutschland sticht kein einzelner Faktor als kritisch hervor: Die meiste Aufmerksamkeit verdient die Säule Naturgefahren mit 6.7/10.
findings.problem: Self-contradicting answer on most scored pages: 'kein einzelner Faktor sticht hervor' is followed by naming the one pillar that deserves 'die meiste Aufmerksamkeit'. Same on AGO ('Gesundheit mit 4.9/10') and ESP ('Naturgefahren mit 6.9/10').
findings.expected: Either name the one pillar that matters most or say that no pillar is in a risk band. Not both.
findings.verification: opus: 'Für Deutschland sticht kein einzelner Faktor als kritisch hervor: Die meiste Aufmerksamkeit verdient die Säule Naturgefahren mit 6.7/10' is coherent: no pillar is critical, yet one is still the relatively weakest. AGO's 4.9 is in the site's 'Moderat' band, so 'nicht kritisch' matches its own labels. The objection is stylistic.

findings.quote: COMPARISON HEADING: Wie sicher ist Aruba im Vergleich zu Nachbarländern und Ländern in der Nähe?
findings.problem: Sixteen grey pages carry a comparison heading ('Wie sicher ist X im Vergleich ...') although they have no score, no rank, and, per the accepted list, no comparison table. The heading promises a comparison the page does not give. Pages: ABW, AIA, ALA, AND, ASM, BES, BLM, CCK, COK, CUW, CXR, CYM, ESH, FRO, GGY, GIB.
findings.expected: Hide the comparison heading on grey pages, or replace it with a one-line note that no comparison is available.
findings.verification: opus: The claim is wrong. ABW.de and AIA.de do show a comparison table under that heading: the place itself with dashes, then scored nearby countries (Grenada, Dominikanische Republik, Venezuela, Haiti). So the heading delivers what it promises. The grey page having a table at all may conflict with the stated design, but that is not what this finding reports.

findings.quote: Sobald für ein Land 30 Stimmen aus mindestens 3 Herkunftsländern vorliegen
findings.problem: Future conditional although China already has 73 votes from 13 countries, and the +0.4 community adjustment is applied in the same block. It reads as if the threshold were not yet reached.
findings.expected: Use the present tense for a place already over the threshold, e.g. 'Ab 30 Stimmen aus mindestens 3 Herkunftsländern ...', or state that the adjustment is active.
findings.verification: opus: The text is in CHN.de's community block, but 'Sobald für ein Land 30 Stimmen ... vorliegen, können ... verschieben' is correct German for a general rule. The same block shows the adjustment as active (+0.4), so nothing contradicts it. This is a stylistic preference at most.

findings.quote: unsicherheitsgewichtetes (Bayesian Shrinkage) geometrisches Mittel
findings.problem: Untranslated English term inside the German methodology sentence [B2], which appears on 192 pages.
findings.expected: Drop the English term and keep 'unsicherheitsgewichtetes geometrisches Mittel', or use a German term.
findings.verification: opus: The phrase is in boilerplate B2 (for example on DEU.de). Putting the English technical term in parentheses is common in German technical writing, and the methodology boilerplate is accepted as intentional. This is a style preference only.

findings.quote: Der schwächste Bereich ist die Korruption: V-Dem bewertet die politische Korruption mit 0,75
findings.problem: Same page: DESCRIPTION says „Hauptrisiko: Regierungsführung (4.2).“ and PILLAR BARS say „Regierungsführung 4.2/10“, which is 3.5 points below the next pillar (Gesundheit 7.7). The SUMMARY instead calls a sub-indicator the weakest area (V-Dem corruption, 0,75 on a 0–1 scale where 1 is strongest) and never mentions the 4.2 pillar.
findings.expected: SUMMARY names the same weakest pillar as DESCRIPTION (Regierungsführung 4.2/10). Corruption can appear as the indicator behind that pillar.
findings.verification: opus: The MKD SUMMARY names the indicator that drives the weakest pillar: political corruption is a V-Dem sub-indicator of Regierungsführung (4.2), which is also the DESCRIPTION's Hauptrisiko. This is consistent, not contradictory. The reviewer also misread the scale: in the table it is 'niedriger ist besser', so 0.75 means high corruption.

findings.quote: Ist Guinea sicher? Score 5.7/10 (2026)
findings.problem: 'Score' is English in the German TITLE of about 65 scored pages (e.g. GIN, GRD, KHM). German titles would use 'Sicherheitswert' or 'Bewertung'. Low severity, but it is the first line readers and search results show.
findings.expected: 'Ist Guinea sicher? Sicherheitswert 5.7/10 (2026)'
findings.verification: opus: 'Ist Guinea sicher? Score 5.7/10 (2026)' is on the page, but 'Score' is an established anglicism in German (it is in Duden) and common in German titles. This is a stylistic preference, not an error.

findings.quote: Der Wert ist ein unsicherheitsgewichtetes (Bayesian Shrinkage) geometrisches Mittel aus fünf Säulen
findings.problem: The English term '(Bayesian Shrinkage)' sits in German text in a boilerplate sentence that appears on 192 pages.
findings.expected: Use a German rendering (e.g. 'Bayes-Schrumpfung') or drop the English term. A native editor should confirm the wording.
findings.verification: opus: '(Bayesian Shrinkage)' is a parenthetical technical term inside intentional methodology boilerplate. Keeping the English statistical term is acceptable in German technical writing, and it is neither factually wrong nor broken.

findings.quote: Die stärkste Säule von Somalia ist Gesundheit (4.1/10)
findings.problem: On 7 pages the strongest pillar is below 6.0 and is still called 'die stärkste Säule' or 'am stärksten', on pages rated 'Nicht empfohlen' or 'hohes Risiko': SOM Gesundheit 4.1 (FAQ2: 'in diesem Bereich ist Somalia am stärksten'), SDN Naturgefahren 5.0, SSD Naturgefahren 5.2, YEM Naturgefahren 5.1, SYR Gesundheit 5.5, TCD Naturgefahren 5.7, VEN Kriminalität 5.6. Health pillars of 7.7 to 8.1 are called the strongest on PRK (7.7), RUS (8.1) and UKR (7.0), where governance is 2.4 to 4.2 on the same page. That pattern suggests the top pillar may reflect thin data rather than real strength.
findings.expected: Use 'stärkste' only when the top pillar is clearly strong. For a best-of-weak pillar say 'am wenigsten schlecht' together with its number. Review the health and hazard inputs behind these top pillars.
findings.verification: opus: 'Die stärkste Säule von Somalia ist Gesundheit (4.1/10)' is literally true and prints the low number next to it. Calling a best-of-weak pillar 'stärkste' is a stylistic preference. The suggestion that RUS/PRK health values come from thin data is speculation the page does not support.

findings.quote: Der schwächste Bereich ist die Korruption: V-Dem bewertet die politische Korruption mit 0,79 auf einer Skala von 0 bis 1, wobei 1 die stärkste ist
findings.problem: The SUMMARY calls corruption 'der schwächste Bereich', yet its own value (0,79 on a scale where 1 is the strongest) sits near the strong end. The page's weakest pillar, Regierungsführung 4.5/10, is the 'Hauptrisiko' in DESCRIPTION but is not mentioned in the SUMMARY. SVK has a similar line ('Der schwächste Bereich ist eine wenig unparteiische Verwaltung: V-Dem bewertet … mit 0,30 …'), where 'eine wenig unparteiische Verwaltung' is also clumsy German.
findings.expected: Name the weakest pillar (Regierungsführung 4.5/10) in the SUMMARY and present corruption as a sub-indicator, explaining the scale direction. A sub-indicator called weakest needs a score on the same basis as the pillars.
findings.verification: opus: In SRB.de 'wobei 1 die stärkste ist' means 1 = strongest corruption, and the indicator table confirms the scale is 'niedriger ist besser'. 0,79 is therefore high corruption and consistent with 'schwächster Bereich'. Corruption is a governance sub-indicator, and governance (4.5) is the weakest pillar, so there is no contradiction. The wording is ambiguous at most.

findings.quote: Wie sicher ist Puerto Rico im Vergleich zu Nachbarländern und Ländern in der Nähe?
findings.problem: Grey pages are meant to show no comparison table, but 13 of the 18 grey pages still print the 'Wie sicher ist X im Vergleich zu Nachbarländern …' heading (PRI, REU, SJM, SMR, SXM, TCA, TKL, UMI, VAT, VGB, VIR, WLF, XKX). PCN, PYF, SGS, SHN and SPM omit it, so the template is inconsistent and the heading promises a comparison that is not shown.
findings.expected: Suppress the comparison heading on every grey page.
findings.verification: owner correction 2026-10-15: By design, not a defect: a grey (partial-data) place keeps its neighbour comparison table, with its own row shown as 'Partial data' next to scored neighbours (src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows). The audit brief wrongly listed 'no comparison table' among the accepted grey-page traits, and the verifier confirmed against that brief. Verifier had said: 47 of the 56 grey de pages render a comparison table: neighbour rows with scores, plus a dashed row for the grey place (e.g. PRI, REU, UMI, VIR). ComparisonTable is rendered unconditionally in CountryPageBody.astro:136, while TrendChart is gated on `scored`. Grey pages without nearby data (PCN, SGS) omit it only because of geography. The design says grey pages have no comparison table. The reviewer is wrong that nothing is shown: the table is shown, and that is the bug.

findings.quote: Wenn eine Mehrheit der Regierungen eine Nicht-reisen-Warnung ausspricht, wird der Gesamtwert von Sudan deutlich nach unten gezogen
findings.problem: Nine 'Nicht empfohlen' or 'hohes Risiko' pages (PRK, PSE, RUS, SDN, SOM, SSD, SYR, UKR, YEM) state a majority trigger. The code has none. src/pipeline/scoring/engine.ts (advisoryConsensus) computes severeShare as a tier-weighted share of L4 advisories, damps it by nAdv/(nAdv+N_SEV) and gates it with rampFactor(nAdv, severeMinNAdv, gateRampWidth); composeScore then applies severeFactor = clamp(1 − S_MAX·severeEff, 0, 1). The effect is proportional to the share, with no 50 % cut-off, so the sentence misdescribes the mechanism.
findings.expected: Describe it as proportional and damped by the number of sources, e.g. 'Je größer der Anteil der Regierungen ist, die von jeder Reise abraten, desto stärker wirkt das auf den Gesamtwert; bei wenigen Quellen wird der Effekt gedämpft.'
findings.verification: opus: The sentence on SDN is quoted correctly (country-faq-copy.ts key a3Cap). It states a sufficient condition: a majority of do-not-travel advisories does pull the score down markedly, since severeFactor = 1 − 0.32·severeShare·nAdv/(nAdv+6). It does not claim a 50% cut-off. Methodology wording that is simplified but not false is accepted.

findings.quote: (1/30 Stimmen, 0/3 Herkunftsländer)
findings.problem: The community line reports one vote from zero origin countries. Votes store the voter's country, so one vote should map to at least one origin country, and the two numbers disagree.
findings.expected: Count origin countries from the same vote set (at least 1 when there is at least 1 vote), or omit the origin count when it is unavailable.
findings.verification: opus: TUN shows '(1/30 Stimmen, 0/3 Herkunftsländer)', but sentiment/aggregate.ts counts only known origins and excludes the UNKNOWN_ORIGIN group (types.ts:339). A vote with unknown country therefore gives 1 vote and 0 origins by design, so the numbers do not contradict each other.

findings.quote: Am meisten Aufmerksamkeit verdient die Gewaltkriminalität: 8,0 Tötungsdelikte je 100.000 Einwohner (Weltbank, 2022).
findings.problem: The headline concern on a page marked 'Zuletzt aktualisiert: 15. Oktober 2026' is a homicide rate from 2022. The year is shown, so it is not hidden, but the sentence presents four-year-old data as the current main risk. TTO ('40,4 Tötungsdelikte je 100.000 Einwohner (Weltbank, 2022)'), ZAF ('43,7 … (Weltbank, 2022)') and VCT ('51,3 … (Weltbank, 2023)') do the same, while other pages cite 'Mordrate (Weltbank)' without a year.
findings.expected: Use the latest homicide year available, or say explicitly that the concern rests on the 2022 figure and that newer data is not yet available.
findings.verification: opus: The 2026-10-15 World Bank raw data holds wb_homicide for SYC, TTO and ZAF with year 2022, and for VCT with 2023. These are the latest values available, and the page states the year explicitly. That is not stale data presented as current.

findings.quote: Community-Stimmung Community Noch nicht genügend Stimmen
findings.problem: The COMMUNITY heading repeats the word 'Community' on every page (also in the grey-page HERO).
findings.expected: 'Community-Stimmung: Noch nicht genügend Stimmen …'
findings.verification: opus: The second 'Community' is the sentiment.badge pill rendered by SentimentPillar.astro:115 next to the 'Community-Stimmung' heading. The repetition appears only in the flattened text extraction, not as broken running text on the page.

findings.quote: - Puerto Rico | Partial data | – | – | – | – | –
findings.problem: 13 grey pages (no official score) still render a comparison table whose own row reads 'Partial data', with scored neighbours beneath it: PRI, VAT, XKX, TCA, SXM, VGB, VIR, SMR, SJM, REU, UMI, TKL, WLF. The accepted rule in this brief says grey places have 'no comparison table', but src/lib/comparisons.ts says grey subjects keep their table ('Data coverage filters the CANDIDATES, never the page'). The rule and the code disagree. Result: 'How does Puerto Rico compare to neighbouring and nearby countries?' is answered with no Puerto Rico figure, while the five grey pages without a table (PCN, PYF, SGS, SHN, SPM) show nothing for the same question.
findings.expected: Pick one rule. Either drop the comparison table on grey pages, as the accepted rule says, or keep it and reword the heading so it does not promise a comparison the subject cannot make. Then align the rule and the code.
findings.verification: owner correction 2026-10-15: By design, not a defect: a grey (partial-data) place keeps its neighbour comparison table, with its own row shown as 'Partial data' next to scored neighbours (src/lib/comparisons.ts comparisonRows). The audit brief wrongly listed 'no comparison table' among the accepted grey-page traits, and the verifier confirmed against that brief. Verifier had said: PRI, REU, SJM and UMI pages render a comparison table whose subject row is 'Partial data | – | ...', while PCN, SGS and SHN have none. comparisons.ts explicitly keeps tables for thin-data subjects, which contradicts the stated grey rule ('no comparison table').

findings.problem: Mauritius and Madagascar are untagged 'neighbours' of the Seychelles (static entry SYC: ['MDG', 'MUS']), about 1,540 km and 1,560 km from the Seychelles point, and the Seychelles has no land border. Both entries are one-sided: neither Mauritius nor Madagascar lists the Seychelles, so their own pages never show it.
findings.expected: Confirm the EEZ boundaries. If they are not adjacent, remove the entries or tag them 'nearby' (and drop any beyond the radius). If they are adjacent, add the reverse entries.
findings.verification: opus: The Seychelles' outer islands (Aldabra group, Mascarene plateau) give it adjacent maritime zones with Madagascar and Mauritius, so SYC: ['MDG','MUS'] is defensible; distance from the Mahé point is irrelevant. The claim that their own pages 'never show it' is false: the MUS and MDG pages both list 'Seychelles nearby'.

findings.quote: The main concern is the spread of epidemics: 4.2 out of 10
findings.problem: The 'main concern' sentence names a risk that is not the lowest-rated pillar. Governance is the lowest pillar on 15 of the 22 scored pages in this batch, and on 13 of them the sentence names something else. AZE names epidemics while PILLAR BARS shows 'Governance 2.9/10'; BGD names 'poor public safety' while 'Governance 3.5/10' is lowest; BLR, BDI and BHR name 'a climate of violence and insecurity' while Governance is 3.8, 2.5 and 4.2. The same mismatch appears on AFG, AGO, ALB, ARG, ARM, ATG, BLZ and BOL. The selection appears to skip the Governance pillar.
findings.expected: Name the lowest-rated pillar as the main concern (for AZE, something like 'The main concern is governance: 2.9/10 ...') and choose from all five pillars, governance included. The sentence should match PILLAR BARS.
findings.verification: opus: The AZE quote is on the page, but naming a risk other than Governance is deliberate. selectDriverPillar in src/lib/country-summary.ts limits the driver to the direct-risk pillars (conflict, crime, health, hazards) and ranks them by weighted drag. It names governance only when all direct-risk pillars are 7.0 or above, as BGR and BIH do ('The weakest area is corruption'). This answers the blogger's 'biggest concern is governance' complaint, so it is not a defect.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor public safety: the Global Peace Index rates safety and security at 2.58
findings.problem: The summary calls public safety the main concern, but the page's own table shows 'Natural hazard exposure (INFORM) | 8.1 / 10', the highest natural-hazard exposure in this batch, plus 'Ongoing disasters (ReliefWeb) | 3' and 'Orange and red disaster alerts (GDACS) | 2'. The Natural hazards pillar is 4.6/10, second-lowest after Governance 3.5/10. The crime pillar (5.7/10) is only third-lowest. A traveller reading the summary is pointed at the wrong risk, and natural-hazard exposure is never mentioned.
findings.expected: Name natural hazards (exposure 8.1/10, 3 ongoing disasters, 2 orange/red alerts) or governance as the main concern, consistent with PILLAR BARS and the indicator table.
findings.verification: opus: The BGD quote is there. Choosing crime (5.7, weight 25%) over natural hazards (4.6, weight 10%) is the documented weighted-drag rule: 0.25·-ln(0.568)=0.141 beats 0.10·-ln(0.457)=0.078. The summary does not contradict the table, and choosing poor public safety as the main concern is defensible.

findings.quote: US State Department: Level 2 (Exercise Increased Caution)
findings.problem: Uncertain. Antarctica is not a country with its own government, and I could not confirm that the US State Department publishes a travel advisory for it. The five listed advisories (Canada, US, Netherlands, New Zealand, France) may be mapped from other territories or be placeholders. The page is 'Partial data', so no score is affected, but it still reports 'Travel advisories from 5 governments' as coverage.
findings.expected: Verify each mapping. Remove any advisory that does not cover Antarctica and update the count in the HERO.
findings.verification: opus: Canada (travel.gc.ca/destinations/antarctica), New Zealand SafeTravel, the Netherlands and the US State Department (destination.ata.html) do publish travel information for Antarctica. The entries come from those issuers' own Antarctica pages, not from placeholders or other territories.

findings.quote: The main concern is poor access to health care: 6.2 out of 10
findings.problem: The summary names health care as the main concern, but the page's own PILLAR BARS show Governance 3.2/10 as the lowest pillar (Health is 5.6/10). The INFORM Governance row (7.7/10, higher is worse) and the V-Dem rule of law row (0.18) are both worse than the 6.2 named.
findings.expected: Name the lowest pillar (Governance 3.2/10) or its worst indicator, not health care at 6.2.
findings.verification: opus: The quote is on COM.en, but the summary deliberately leaves governance out of the main concern. selectDriverPillar in src/lib/country-summary.ts names governance only when every direct-risk pillar is at 7+, and it skips pillars with too little data (Crime has 0% coverage). This answers the blogger's 'biggest concern is governance' complaint, and the same pattern is covered (and rejected) under #4. Separate real issue not raised here: COM's FAQ Q1 says the score is pulled down 'above all by governance (3.2/10)' while the summary names health.

findings.quote: The main concern is violent crime: 17.7 homicides per 100,000 people
findings.problem: The main-concern sentence often names a risk other than the lowest pillar bar. CRI names violent crime (Crime 6.7/10) while Natural hazards 5.2/10 is lowest. CUB names 'poor public safety' while Governance 3.2/10 is lowest. CMR names armed conflict while Governance 2.4/10 is lowest. BRB names epidemics while Natural hazards 6.2/10 is lowest. Governance is never named as the main concern, even on the pages where it is the lowest bar (COM, CUB, CMR, COD, COG, CHN, DJI, CIV).
findings.expected: Derive the main-concern sentence from the same lowest-pillar logic as the bars, or state that the sentence names the worst single indicator and show that indicator.
